source: BK5-6 printed pp.2-3 = book5-6.pdf PDF pp.8-9 (rule p.2 = PDF p.8, program and procedure p.3 = PDF p.9), image-read; Step 7 speculative derivation from topology
note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A): every expect is derived by hand from the 16-wire topology and the p.2 rule, not printed. No erratum touches this program. Topology: relay 6 coil runs 6C(+)-indicator lamp 6-6E-coil-6F; 6F reaches minus through pushbutton 1 N.O. (1X/1Y, 1Y/2Y/2-) to set, and through its own set 2 N.O. 6L-6K plus the series N.C. chain of pushbuttons 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (6Z..2Y on minus) to hold. Relay 6 set 1 (6H on minus, 6J N.C.) puts 5J at minus when relay 6 is out: light 5 (5A at +, 5B/5J) is the alarm, and relay 5's coil (5E at +) feeds through its own N.C. contact 5F-5H-5J and self-interrupts, so relay 5 is asserted only at rest (set state), never while the alarm is on; relay 5's indicator lamp hangs on the unwired 5C and stays dark. Script choices, not printed: pushbutton 3 is the held-and-released case, pushbuttons 2, 4 and 5 are each pushed and released after a re-set, and pushbutton 6 is held while pushbutton 1 is pushed and released (the p.2 'closing the contacts and throwing a re-set switch' case). Powered phases with relay 6 out use fixed advances instead of settle, because relay 5 buzzes; the 200 ms advance after each set lets light 5's filament cool, as in V-EXP2, and is not from the source.

script.cite: BK5-6 printed p.3 = book5-6.pdf PDF p.9 procedure; derived from topology: at cold start relay 6 is unoperated and 6F has no path to minus (1X N.O. open, 6K N.O. open), so the coil and its series indicator lamp 6 carry nothing; 6H(-)-6J closed puts 5J at minus and light 5 (5A at +) lights; relay 5's indicator lamp hangs on the unwired 5C, so it stays dark while its coil (fed from 5E at +) runs through 5F-5H-5J
script.quote: Turn power ON. The alarm (light 5) comes ON.

script.cite: BK5-6 printed p.3 = book5-6.pdf PDF p.9 procedure, re-set button held; derived from topology: pushbutton 1 N.O. 1X(6F)-1Y(-) pulls relay 6 directly; relay 6 coil 6C(+)-indicator lamp 6-6E-coil-6F, 6F reaching minus through 6L-6K (relay 6 set 2 N.O.) and the series N.C. chain 6Z-6Y-5Z-5Y-4Z-4Y-3Z-3Y-2Z-2Y(-); 6H-6J open, so 5J (light 5 at 5B, relay 5 contact arm path 5F-5H-5J) has no path to minus: light 5 dark, relay 5 coil (5E at +) unfed and at rest
script.quote: Set the system by pushing the re-set button (pushbutton 1). The burglar alarm is now set.

script.quote: Set the system by pushing the re-set button (pushbutton 1). The burglar alarm is now set.

script.cite: BK5-6 printed p.2 = book5-6.pdf PDF p.8 rule, pushbutton 3 held; derived from topology: the pushed button opens its N.C. Y-Z contact, breaking the only hold path from 6F to minus (pushbutton 1 N.O. 1X open), so relay 6 drops and 6H(-)-6J closes; light 5 (5A at +, 5B on 5J) lights through 6J-6H; relay 5's indicator lamp (5C unwired) stays dark
script.quote: The program which follows illustrates a simple alarm circuit. If any contact is broken by pushing any of pushbuttons 2 through 6, the alarm (light 5) comes on. The system is re-set by pushing pushbutton 1.
